name: BMW World Championship
epitaph: Risk won it from Jeremiah Wilson at Trial And Error (27 Jan 2002) with an assist from Axel Teflon; Billy Blaze held it through an unrecorded change somewhere in the following months before Tax pinned Risk in a triple threat at Money, Power, Respect II (28 Jul 2002) to end Blaze's own three-month reign — and carried it, still champion, into a mid-August title defense against 'Tank' Hank Gunyon and Reality whose result the surviving record never shows.
notes: The Blaze-regains-the-title transition between Risk's Trial And Error win and his own reign as champion by Money, Power, Respect II is not evidenced anywhere in the held record — an honest gap, not an inferred date.

name: Million Dollar Championship
epitaph: Axel Teflon defended it against Kid Krazie at Trial And Error (27 Jan 2002), ending Krazie's own career; by Money, Power, Respect II (28 Jul 2002) it belonged to ICE, unrecorded in between, and changed hands there to Da Thug when ICE's own ex-girlfriend Kelly set him on fire mid-pinfall — Da Thug still champion at the record's own end.

name: Blood Money Championship
epitaph: Reaper defended it at Trial And Error (27 Jan 2002) against Dr. Doyle Van Helsing in a two-arena hardcore key hunt; the fed's own Money, Power, Respect II recap (28 Jul 2002) names Violent B the new champion out of a Krisis-and-Violent-B-vs.-Tank-and-J-Man tag match whose own text never actually shows Violent B taking a fall or a pin — a title change the surviving record asserts without fully narrating.
notes: The corpus never shows the title passing from Reaper to Violent B directly — an honest gap between the two recorded reigns.

name: Cash Money Championship
epitaph: Mark Espinosa lost it to The Underlord at Trial And Error (27 Jan 2002); The Underlord — also billed as 'Mafia Man' Mario Ghotti — carried it at least through a non-title FallOut main event before Paranoia won a three-way for it at Money, Power, Respect II (28 Jul 2002), still champion when 'The Violence' Vince Jones and Raymond Mercy debuted by jumping him the same night, and still champion as of the last dated reference the corpus holds (mid-August).

name: Cruiserweight Championship
epitaph: Chilly K, billed as its own 'first substantial' champion, defended it against The SensationalSal One at Trial And Error (27 Jan 2002) and lost a non-title rematch to Eiji Fujiwara at FallOut without the belt changing hands — the only reign the surviving record evidences.

name: BMW Tag Team Championship
epitaph: Vacant entering Money, Power, Respect II (28 Jul 2002) per the fed's own recap; 2GLS (Reality and Jeremiah Wilson) won it there off Big Money Legends (Kid Krazie and Scott Phillips) in an Inferno Tables match, both teams sent through burning tables before the finish.
notes: The vacancy itself — who held it before, and why — is not evidenced anywhere in the held record.

name: Top Dollar Championship
epitaph: Revealed 'back' on air by Da Mab on 2 August 2002 as part of Louis Miranda's new stable's own announced plans — the surviving record names no holder, before or after.
notes: No reign structured; the belt is shown, not awarded, in what this pass read.
